title: Sudden severe headache
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in the Emergency Department. Rachel Green, 45, presents with a headache. Take a focused history to identify the cause and any red flags. You may use the Examine and Investigations panels. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: Rachel Green
patient.setting: Emergency Department cubicle, lights dimmed at her request.
patient.openingStatement: I've got the most horrendous headache. It came on out of nowhere a few hours ago.
patient.demeanour: In obvious pain, holding her head, eyes half-closed, prefers the lights low. Speaks slowly and quietly.
patient.speechStyle: Quiet, slow, short answers. Everyday language: 'like being hit with a bat'.

ice.ideas: Wonders if it's a bad migraine, though she doesn't usually get them.
ice.concerns: Scared it might be something serious like a bleed, as she's never had anything like it.
ice.expectations: Wants the pain to stop and to know what it is.

freelyShared: It started about four hours ago while she was at the gym lifting weights.
It's the worst headache she's ever had.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: how quickly it came on or how fast it reached maximum
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: It was instant — like being hit on the back of the head with a bat. Full strength within seconds.
keywords: hit on the back of the head

revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: My neck feels really stiff and the lights hurt my eyes.
I was sick in the car on the way here.
The lady at the gym said I went a bit vacant for a moment, but I didn't pass out completely.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: weakness, numbness, vision or speech changes, seizures
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: No weakness or numbness. My vision's okay, just the light bothers me.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: smoking, blood pressure, family history, medications
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I smoke about ten a day. My blood pressure's a bit high, I'm on amlodipine. My aunt died suddenly of a brain bleed in her forties.
No fever, no rash, I was well this morning.
I get the odd tension headache but nothing remotely like this.

patient.cue: I've honestly never had anything like it. Should I be worried?

examFindings.finding: HR 64, BP 178/98, RR 16, SpO2 98%, temperature 37.0°C, GCS 15.
Neck stiffness present, Kernig's sign positive. Pupils equal and reactive. No focal neurological deficit. Fundi: no papilloedema.

investigations.result: Hyperdensity in the basal cisterns and Sylvian fissures.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis and which features support it?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Subarachnoid haemorrhage: thunderclap onset during exertion, worst-ever headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting, brief altered consciousness, smoking, hypertension and family history.
keyPoints: Risk factors: smoking, hypertension, family history

postEncounterQuestions.q: What are the next steps in management?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Urgent senior and neurosurgical referral, CT angiography, nimodipine, analgesia and antiemetics, blood pressure control, neuro observations; lumbar puncture for xanthochromia if CT had been negative beyond 6 hours.

items.text: Introduces self, gains consent and adapts to her discomfort (e.g. lights)
Establishes speed of onset (thunderclap) and activity at onset
items.evidenceHint: how quickly, what were you doing

items.text: Characterises site, severity and progression of the headache
Asks about neck stiffness, photophobia and vomiting
Asks about loss of consciousness, seizures and focal neurological symptoms
Asks about risk factors: hypertension, smoking, family history, anticoagulants
Addresses her worry honestly and explains next steps
